name: Anras
kurzbeschreibung: Historic community in the Pustertal with Schloss Anras and the baroque parish church.
beschreibung:
Overview

Anras is situated at an elevation of 1,261 meters on an expansive sunny mountain terrace along the southern slopes of the Villgraten Mountains in East Tyrol's Hochpustertal, perched high above the Drau River valley. Home to approximately 1,250 residents in the district of Lienz, the municipality encompasses the historic village center along with the communities of Asch, Ried, Mittewald an der Drau, Kosteberg, and Goll. Blessed with exceptional sunshine and fertile slopes, Anras was renowned for centuries as the 'Granary of East Tyrol', successfully cultivating grain at elevations surpassing 1,200 meters. Today, this peaceful mountain village offers pristine rural charm and sweeping panoramas across the Lienz Dolomites and the Carnic Alps.

History

Settlement dates back to antiquity, as evidenced by archaeological excavation of Raetian settlement remains near Anras Castle. By 1020 AD, the Prince-Bishopric of Brixen held estates here, and in 1180 Anras hosted a regional church council and Tyrolean diet. In 1236, Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II granted the Prince-Bishops of Brixen secular jurisdiction over the entire domain of Anras. The historic Pfleghaus castle served as their summer residence and judicial seat, receiving extensive Baroque expansions in 1754 by architect Simon Rieder. Following secularization in 1803, the castle deteriorated until the Messerschmitt Foundation acquired and meticulously restored the monument in 1991. The Baroque parish church of Saint Stephen was constructed between 1753 and 1756 by Franz de Paula Penz.

Getting There

By car from Lienz, take the Drau Valley highway B100 westward toward Sillian for 15 kilometers to Mittewald an der Drau. There, branch onto the Pustertal High Road L324, which winds up through gentle switchbacks to Anras in about ten minutes. From South Tyrol, drivers follow the B100 east from Innichen to Mittewald. By rail, travelers take the Drau Valley railway to Mittewald an der Drau station, served hourly by trains linking Lienz with San Candido and Franzensfeste. VVT regional bus line 962 connects directly from the station to Anras village square in under ten minutes.

Tips

The centerpiece is historic Schloss Anras, today an acclaimed cultural center featuring the restored 1755 courtroom, timber-paneled chambers, and art exhibitions. Adjacent stands Saint Stephen's Parish Church, celebrated for its 1754 ceiling frescoes by young master Martin Knoller, displaying breathtaking trompe-l'œil Rococo architecture. Outdoor enthusiasts can explore the scenic Pustertal High Road, hike to the hospitable Anraser Alm, summit Mount Spitzenstein (2,265 m) for panoramic vistas of the Dolomites, or venture into the untamed Kristeinertal valley. Village taverns serve authentic East Tyrolean delicacies such as potato-stuffed Schlipfkrapfen.
